title: Exploring the Role of Myostatin Mutation on Microstructure and Crystallography of Quail Eggs Using SEM and EBSD Techniques
content: Eggshell integrity is a crucial factor in poultry farming, impacting both food security and disease control. Myostatin (MSTN) is a key regulator of muscle growth, with MSTN mutant poultry exhibiting increased muscle mass and reduced fat deposition [1]. While its role in muscle growth is well understood across species, its role in avian eggshell formation remains unclear. Investigating this connection could provide new insights into the genetic and structural mechanisms governing eggshell biomineralization. We present our scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) study on genetically engineered poultry eggshells to comprehensively examine the effects of MSTN mutation on biomineralization, microstructure, and crystallographic orientation that impact the surface properties and mechanical strength of the eggshells.
